    Showcase — the Horn of Africa drought (CHIRPS rainfall)¶

    From 2020 the Horn of Africa endured its worst drought in decades as successive rainy seasons failed. CHIRPS (Climate Hazards Center) is the standard quasi-global rainfall dataset for drought monitoring. This notebook uses the earthlens CHC backend to pull CHIRPS monthly rainfall for the March–May long-rains season and compares the failed 2022 season against a normal year, mapping the rainfall deficit.

    Runs a live CHIRPS FTP download (anonymous, no credentials).

    What this notebook does¶

    1. Download CHIRPS monthly rainfall through earthlens for the March-May long-rains season of a normal year (2018) and the failed 2022 season.
    2. Sum each season to a rainfall total.
    3. Map the deficit and report the average shortfall.

    CHIRPS is the standard quasi-global rainfall dataset for drought monitoring; the CHC backend fetches it over anonymous FTP and returns the written GeoTIFF paths.

    Running it. This makes a real CHIRPS FTP download — no credentials required.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    # --- Helper: download CHIRPS Mar-May monthly rainfall and sum to a season total ---
# CHC returns the written monthly GeoTIFFs; we read them with pyramids, mask the
# no-data (< 0), and sum the three months into one seasonal-total grid.
import os, tempfile
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from loguru import logger
from earthlens import EarthLens

logger.disable("earthlens"); logger.disable("pyramids")
from pyramids.dataset import Dataset

def mam_total(year):
    """Download CHIRPS Mar–May monthly rainfall and sum to a seasonal total."""
    paths = EarthLens(
        data_source="chc", temporal_resolution="monthly",
        variables=["precipitation"],
        start=f"{year}-03-01", end=f"{year}-05-31",
        lat_lim=[-5.0, 12.0], lon_lim=[38.0, 52.0],  # Horn of Africa
        path=tempfile.mkdtemp(),
    ).download(progress_bar=False)
    stack = [np.asarray(Dataset.read_file(str(p)).read_array(), dtype="float32") for p in paths]
    stack = [s[0] if s.ndim == 3 else s for s in stack]
    arr = np.where(np.array(stack) < 0, np.nan, stack)
    return np.nansum(arr, axis=0)

try:
    wet = mam_total(2018)   # a near-normal long-rains season
    dry = mam_total(2022)   # the failed 2022 season
    print("seasonal rainfall grids:", wet.shape, dry.shape)
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
    wet = dry = None; print("CHIRPS download skipped:", exc)
    # --- Helper: download CHIRPS Mar-May monthly rainfall and sum to a season total --- # CHC returns the written monthly GeoTIFFs; we read them with pyramids, mask the # no-data (< 0), and sum the three months into one seasonal-total grid. import os, tempfile import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt from loguru import logger from earthlens import EarthLens logger.disable("earthlens"); logger.disable("pyramids") from pyramids.dataset import Dataset def mam_total(year): """Download CHIRPS Mar–May monthly rainfall and sum to a seasonal total.""" paths = EarthLens( data_source="chc", temporal_resolution="monthly", variables=["precipitation"], start=f"{year}-03-01", end=f"{year}-05-31", lat_lim=[-5.0, 12.0], lon_lim=[38.0, 52.0], # Horn of Africa path=tempfile.mkdtemp(), ).download(progress_bar=False) stack = [np.asarray(Dataset.read_file(str(p)).read_array(), dtype="float32") for p in paths] stack = [s[0] if s.ndim == 3 else s for s in stack] arr = np.where(np.array(stack) < 0, np.nan, stack) return np.nansum(arr, axis=0) try: wet = mam_total(2018) # a near-normal long-rains season dry = mam_total(2022) # the failed 2022 season print("seasonal rainfall grids:", wet.shape, dry.shape) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 wet = dry = None; print("CHIRPS download skipped:", exc)
    seasonal rainfall grids: (341, 281) (341, 281)

    March–May rainfall: 2018 vs 2022, and the deficit¶

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    # Crop both years to a common shape, map 2018 / 2022 / their difference, and
# print the mean seasonal rainfall and the percentage shortfall.
if wet is not None and dry is not None:
    h = min(wet.shape[0], dry.shape[0]); w = min(wet.shape[1], dry.shape[1])
    wet, dry = wet[:h, :w], dry[:h, :w]
    deficit = dry - wet
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5))
    vm = float(np.nanpercentile(np.concatenate([wet.ravel(), dry.ravel()]), 98))
    ax[0].imshow(wet, cmap="YlGnBu", vmin=0, vmax=vm); ax[0].set_title("MAM rainfall — 2018 (mm)")
    ax[1].imshow(dry, cmap="YlGnBu", vmin=0, vmax=vm); ax[1].set_title("MAM rainfall — 2022 (mm)")
    im = ax[2].imshow(deficit, cmap="BrBG", vmin=-vm, vmax=vm); ax[2].set_title("deficit (2022 − 2018, mm)")
    for a in ax: a.axis("off")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax[2], fraction=0.046, label="mm")
    plt.show()
    print(f"mean MAM rainfall  2018: {np.nanmean(wet):.0f} mm   2022: {np.nanmean(dry):.0f} mm   "
          f"({(np.nanmean(dry)/np.nanmean(wet)-1)*100:+.0f}%)")
else:
    print("no rainfall grids")
    # Crop both years to a common shape, map 2018 / 2022 / their difference, and # print the mean seasonal rainfall and the percentage shortfall. if wet is not None and dry is not None: h = min(wet.shape[0], dry.shape[0]); w = min(wet.shape[1], dry.shape[1]) wet, dry = wet[:h, :w], dry[:h, :w] deficit = dry - wet fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5)) vm = float(np.nanpercentile(np.concatenate([wet.ravel(), dry.ravel()]), 98)) ax[0].imshow(wet, cmap="YlGnBu", vmin=0, vmax=vm); ax[0].set_title("MAM rainfall — 2018 (mm)") ax[1].imshow(dry, cmap="YlGnBu", vmin=0, vmax=vm); ax[1].set_title("MAM rainfall — 2022 (mm)") im = ax[2].imshow(deficit, cmap="BrBG", vmin=-vm, vmax=vm); ax[2].set_title("deficit (2022 − 2018, mm)") for a in ax: a.axis("off") fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax[2], fraction=0.046, label="mm") plt.show() print(f"mean MAM rainfall 2018: {np.nanmean(wet):.0f} mm 2022: {np.nanmean(dry):.0f} mm " f"({(np.nanmean(dry)/np.nanmean(wet)-1)*100:+.0f}%)") else: print("no rainfall grids")
    mean MAM rainfall  2018: 159 mm   2022: 63 mm   (-60%)

    Recap¶

    Differencing two CHIRPS seasons turns a rainfall archive into a drought map and a single deficit figure — exactly how failed rainy seasons are flagged operationally.

    Try it yourself¶

    • Compare other years, or switch to the October-December short rains.
    • Re-point the lat_lim/lon_lim box at any region.
    • See the CHC backend reference.
